name: MPL3115A2R1
title: MPL3115A2: I²C absolute pressure sensor with altimeter and thermometer outputs, 20 to 110 kPa
summary: A piezoresistive MEMS absolute pressure sensor in a 3 mm × 5 mm × 1.1 mm 8-pin LGA with a metal lid and an air vent hole. An on-chip temperature sensor and ADC give compensated pressure in pascals (20-bit, Q18.2), altitude in metres (20-bit signed, Q16.4) or raw counts, plus temperature in °C (12-bit, Q8.4), over I²C at address 0x60. It runs 20 to 110 kPa, is calibrated 50 to 110 kPa, and holds a 32-sample FIFO, min/max and delta registers, threshold and window alarms on two programmable interrupt pins, and an autonomous acquisition timer from 1 s to 9 h. MPL3115A2R1 is the tape-and-reel part; MPL3115A2 ships in trays.

circuits.title: Typical application diagram
circuits.description: The sensor on its own supplies and bus. VDD carries C1, 100 nF, and C2, 10 µF, to ground, both close to pin 1. CAP, the internal regulator's pin, gets its own 100 nF, C3, to ground. VDDIO feeds the interface. SCL comes in, SDA goes both ways and INT1 and INT2 go out to the host.

operation.text: A piezoresistive MEMS element measures pressure against a vacuum sealed in its reference chamber. The on-chip temperature sensor compensates it, and a high-resolution ADC and digital processing deliver pressure in pascals or altitude in metres, and temperature in °C, so the host does no compensation or unit conversion.

Sensitivity and offset for pressure and temperature are trimmed at the factory and kept in NVM; these values load at every power-up and need no further calibration. For best accuracy the offsets can be trimmed after power-up through OFF_P, OFF_T and OFF_H, which are volatile. Using the offset correction to remove board-mount and long-term offset shift is strongly urged to reach the full accuracy. Offset shift cancels in relative measurements, where two absolute readings are subtracted.

ALT in CTRL_REG1 picks the mode. Barometer mode reports 20-bit unsigned pascals; altimeter mode converts to altitude with the US Standard Atmosphere and reports 20-bit two's complement metres. Both modes give temperature as well. Altitude needs the local sea-level pressure written to BAR_IN in 2 Pa units; it resets to 101,326 Pa. Pressure resolves below 1 Pa and altitude better than 1 m at sea level.

With RAW set the ADC result, oversampled but unscaled, fills all 24 bits of OUT_P and all 16 of OUT_T in either mode. The FIFO must be disabled, and alarms, deltas and other interrupts do not run; the delta registers are not updated.

OFF: VDD below 1.62 V, no function. STANDBY (SBYB = 0, the reset state): digital logic and POR run, the analog chain is off, registers can be read and written, 2 µA typ. ACTIVE (SBYB = 1): everything runs and measurements repeat at the ST interval. Inside ACTIVE the part moves between WAKE and SLEEP. CTRL_REG1, CTRL_REG3, CTRL_REG4 and CTRL_REG5 are written only in STANDBY, apart from the SBYB, OST and RST fields. Valid data comes 60 ms max after entering ACTIVE at OSR 1, 1000 ms max at OSR 128.

OS sets an oversample ratio of 1 to 128. More oversampling lowers noise (19 Pa RMS at 1x, 1.5 Pa RMS at 128x) and lengthens the minimum sample spacing from 6 ms to 512 ms, and raises average current at one update per second from 8.5 µA to 265 µA; 40 µA at OSR 16 gives a steady 10 cm resolution. Peak current during a conversion is 2 mA typ.

In STANDBY, setting OST takes one pressure/altitude and temperature reading and returns to STANDBY, clearing OST. In ACTIVE the part acquires every 2^ST seconds, 1 s to 9 h, and can fill the 32-sample FIFO, logging up to about 12 days.

The 32-sample FIFO stores pressure/altitude and temperature together. F_MODE picks off, circular (newest kept) or stop-when-full. With the FIFO on, it is read through address 01h with an I²C burst read, five bytes per sample, oldest first; 02h to 05h read 00h. Overflow and watermark events raise interrupts. TIME_DLY counts sample ticks after overflow.

Eight sources: data ready, FIFO, pressure window, temperature window, pressure threshold, temperature threshold, pressure change and temperature change. CTRL_REG4 enables each, CTRL_REG5 sends each to INT1 or INT2 (INT2 by default), and the sources on one pin are ORed, so the host reads INT_SOURCE to see which fired. Each pin has its own polarity and push-pull or open-drain choice in CTRL_REG3. Status bits set on a rising event and clear when the relevant register is read.

The threshold flag sets when the reading reaches the target in P_TGT or T_TGT; with a non-zero window it also sets at target plus and minus the window, so a 3000 m target with 100 m window fires at 2900, 3000 and 3100 m. The window flag sets while the reading sits within target ± window and never with a zero window. The change flags set when consecutive readings differ by more than the window value. ALARM_SEL and LOAD_OUTPUT can take the targets from the current reading instead of the target registers. In barometer mode targets and windows are pressures in 2 Pa units; in altimeter mode metres.

OUT_P_DELTA and OUT_T_DELTA hold the difference from the previous sample, in the same formats as the outputs, whatever F_MODE is. P_MIN, P_MAX, T_MIN and T_MAX capture extremes; they clear at power-up or when 0 is written.

Slave only, 7-bit address 60h (C0h write, C1h read); other addresses on request from the factory. Up to 400 kHz with 1 kΩ pull-ups at 400 pF, 4 MHz at 20 pF. Reads of a chosen register use a repeated START. Register addresses auto-increment, so STATUS, three pressure bytes and two temperature bytes come out of 00h to 05h in one 6-byte read; the delta block and FIFO have their own wrap points. WHO_AM_I at 0Ch reads C4h.

Example at OSR 128 in altimeter mode: write B8h to CTRL_REG1 (26h), write 07h to PT_DATA_CFG (13h) to enable the data flags, write B9h to CTRL_REG1 to go ACTIVE. Then read STATUS (00h) until bit 3 (08h, PTDR) is set and read 01h to 05h, which clears the data-ready flag.

Same as polling, plus 11h to CTRL_REG3 (28h) for active-low open-drain outputs and 80h to CTRL_REG4 (29h) to enable the data-ready interrupt, before B9h to CTRL_REG1. On an INT2 assertion read INT_SOURCE (12h); if bit 7 (SRC_DRDY) is set read 01h to 05h, otherwise service the other source.
VDD takes 100 nF ceramic plus a 10 µF bulk or ceramic capacitor, as close to pin 1 as possible. CAP takes a separate 100 nF to bypass the internal regulator.

RoHS-compliant LGA with a metal lid and an air vent hole of 0.5 mm diameter in the top. The pin 1 index area on the underside has no electrical connection. The part is sensitive to mechanical shock. NXP notes AN1984 and AN3150 cover handling and soldering of its pressure sensors.
